## Why This Is Asked
Tests for offline sync and conflict resolution are common in fintech and media apps; this checks practical thinking beyond basic unit tests.

## Key Concepts
- Offline storage (IndexedDB)
- Sync strategies (last-write-wins, timestamps)
- Conflict resolution determinism
- End-to-end tooling (MSW, Playwright)
- CI simulation of offline/online

## Code Example
```javascript
function resolveConflict(local, remote) {
  // last-write-wins by timestamp
  if ((local.updatedAt || 0) > (remote.updatedAt || 0)) return local;
  return remote;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test idempotency in syncing?
- How would you handle large sync payloads and partial failures?

## Why This Is Asked

- Multi-tenant data isolation and idempotency

- Observability: OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana

## Code Example

```yaml
# feature flag for canary rollout (illustrative)
apiVersion: flags.example/v1
kind: FeatureFlag
metadata:
  name: chaos-payments-canary
spec:
  enabled: true
  rolloutPercent: 10
```

```go
// idempotent payment retry sketch
func handlePayment(req PaymentRequest) error {
  key := req.IdempotencyKey
  if seen(key) { return nil }
  err := process(req)
  if err != nil { return retryWithBackoff(req) }
  markSeen(key)
  return nil
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt this plan for PCI-DSS/regulatory constraints?
- Which metrics define a safe blast radius and when to halt chaos runs?
